title: Two States Went to War Over Toledo #shorts

lines.text: In 1835, Ohio and Michigan nearly went to war over the city of Toledo.
Both states sent militias, but the only shots were warning shots, and the only casualty was a sheriff stabbed in a tavern brawl.
President Jackson stepped in, and Congress offered Michigan a deal: give up Toledo, and take the Upper Peninsula.
Michiganders called it a worthless wasteland, until it turned out to be full of copper and iron.
So, who really won the Toledo War?

sources: https://www.history.com/news/the-toledo-war-when-michigan-and-ohio-nearly-came-to-blows (dispute over 468 sq mi Toledo Strip, 1835-36; Michigan militia fired warning shots and arrested nine Ohio surveyors at Phillips Corners, no one hurt; Michigan sheriff Joseph Wood stabbed in a tavern brawl July 1835, minor wound, only casualty; Jackson removed Mason, militias stood down; Michigan accepted Congress's deal Dec 14 1836: statehood plus about 9,000 sq mi of the Upper Peninsula; Detroit Free Press called the U.P. a land of perpetual snows; later found to hold copper and iron ore)

https://www.michigan.gov/dmva/about/history/military-events/highlights/the-toledo-war (shots over heads of Ohio officials, surveyors captured, tavern stabbing of a Michigan sheriff, Jackson intervened, Michigan became the 26th state Jan 26 1837 with western three-quarters of the Upper Peninsula)

facts.hedge: script says 'nearly went to war' and 'only shots were warning shots' per both sources
